verdict: CONFIRMED - all four ids matched at 4 independent metrics, in both screenshots, with a large margin over the runner-up.

results.notes: Best match of the four: 88% of the sprite's interior pixels are within 12/255 of the screen. Screen D is a single sprite, NOT a composite of two images.

not_direct_copies.detail: All four avatars ARE direct copies of the sprite: the sprite is drawn with 'contain' fit into a ~94 px box, centred, over a flat dark backdrop (~#272528), then the whole screen was JPEG-compressed and downscaled. Evidence: the difference heatmaps in the evidence images are black everywhere except along the sprite's outlines and internal line art - exactly the signature of resampling. A different image would show large bright blobs inside flat colour regions; a tinted or masked variant would light up in patches.

screen_model.sprite_rendering: contain fit into a ~94 px box, aspect preserved, centred, then sub-pixel aligned

method_summary: For every one of the 1408 library sprites, rebuild the avatar box: fill a flat backdrop sampled from the box border, draw the sprite with contain-fit into a box size that is searched from 84 to 104 px, centred, with sub-pixel offsets searched from -4 to +4. Score = mean absolute RGB difference (0..255) against the real screen pixels. Stage 1 scans all sprites at 32x32 with three box sizes; stage 2 refines the top 30 at 54x54 over box size and offset; stage 3 re-scores the top 8 at native 108x108 and adds alpha-masked statistics; stage 4 repeats the whole thing for B/C/D against the second screenshot. verify_final.ps1 then re-fits from scratch and reports four independent residuals per candidate, including an interior-only residual restricted to pixels whose full 3x3 sprite-mask neighbourhood is opaque, which no resampling artefact can influence.
pitfalls_hit: This machine's 'powershell' is Windows PowerShell 5.1, which decodes a BOM-less .ps1 as GBK; a script containing a Chinese path literal created a mojibake directory D:\<garbage>\miHoYo Launcher. All final scripts are ASCII-only and derive the repo root from $PSScriptRoot.
In PowerShell the comma binds tighter than '-', so @($a-1,$b-1) parses as $a - (1, $b-1) and throws 'op_Subtraction' on System.Object[]. Always parenthesise.
PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive: $W and $w are the same variable. This silently produced a 94x94 evidence canvas.
[System.Drawing.Drawing2D.PixelOffsetMode]::High does not exist on .NET Framework 4.8; use HighQuality.
'Diff' is a built-in alias for Compare-Object, so custom comparison functions must not be named Diff.

Sprites are transparent PNGs. Drawing one onto a fresh Bitmap leaves transparent pixels black, which differs from the on-screen backdrop by 40+; that is exactly why the earlier match_avatar2.ps1 reported meaningless 37-49 differences and never hit any known id. You must fill the backdrop (or compare only opaque pixels).
